Inglewood, California
  March 12, 2019

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
March 12, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
APPOINTMENT OF MAYOR PRO TEM. It was moved by Council Member
Franklin, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the City Council does hereby
appoint Council Member Morales as Mayor Pro Tem. The motion was carried by the
following roll call vote:
Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Franklin, and Council Member Morales;
Noes: None; and
Absent: Mayor Butts.

Mayor Pro Tem Morales called the City Council into session for Closed Session at the
hour of 1:01 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Pro Tem Morales, Council Members Dotson,
  Padilla, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  Mayor Butts.

City officials and personnel present for Closed Session were as follows:

  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item.

There was no response.

Mayor Pro Tem Morales recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed
Session Item No. CS-1.

  **********************************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority Secretary
announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
  Chairman/Joint  Powers  Authority  Chairman
  Butts/Council  Members/Successor  Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members/Finance Authority
  Members/Parking Authority Members/Joint Powers
  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales and
  Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.

  1
 March 12, 2019

  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint
  Powers Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Wanda Brown  City Treasurer/Treasurer*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance Authority,
  Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
  present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
  Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on
  the Agenda.

  There was no response.

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Dotson that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  March 7, 2019, in the amount of $2,520,051.90, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending denial
  of the following claims:
  a) Century National Insurance for alleged property damage on January 20, 2018.
  b) De’Antre Henderson for alleged property damage on January 21, 2019.
  c) Roman Johnson for denial of a building permit on November 21, 2018.
  d) Glen Livingston for alleged property damage on December 8, 2018.
  e) Pacific Bell/AT&T for alleged property damage on August 13, 2018.
  f) Joseph Taylor for alleged property damage on December 13, 2018.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Dotson, and
  carried that the above listed claim be denied.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales and seconded by Council
  Member Dotson that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on February 26,
  2019, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 301  AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 18-205 APPROVED – JLEE
  ENGINEERING, INC. Staff report dated March 12, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval of an amendment to Agreement No. 18-205 with JLee
  Engineering, Inc., extending the term of the contract to September 30, 2020, and
  increasing the total compensation by an additional $150,000 to continue providing
  Building Safety inspection services.

  2
 March 12, 2019

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve the amendment. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 101  AGREEMENT NO. 19-137(A) APPROVED – VISIBLE GRAPHICS, INC.; USE
  OF TAX EXEMPT BOND FUNDS AUTHORIZED. Staff report dated March 12,
  2019, was presented recommending approval of an agreement with Visible Graphics,
  Inc., to fabricate and install signage on each floor of Parking Garage #2 located at 115
  South Locust Street.

  It was moved by Council Member/Successor Agency Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member Dotson that the City Council/Successor
  Agency does hereby 1) Approve Agreement No. 19-137(A) in the amount of $19,045;
  and 2) Authorize the Mayor/Chairman to execute Agreement No. 19-137(A). The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin
  and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Successor Agency Member Morales, and seconded by Successor
  Agency Member Dotson that the Successor Agency does hereby approve the use of tax-
  exempt bond funds for the work to be performed by Visible Graphics, Inc. (as required
  by the Agreement) in a total contract amount of $19,045. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Successor
  Agency Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 132.6  CLOSED SESSION – DAISY BECERRA VS. CITY OF INGLEWOOD Closed
  session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged; Conference with Legal Counsel;
  Pending Litigation; Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1); Name of Case: Daisy
  Beccerra vs. City of Inglewood, et al; LASC Case No. BC693689.

  Discussion Held; Direction Given to Staff

 219  ORAL REPORTS – CITY TREASURER. City Treasurer, Wanda Brown, gave a brief
  report on the Freddy Mack Bond she purchased. She also invited the community to
  attend the Treasurer’s Community Workshop at City Hall on April 27, 2019, in
  Community Room A from 10:00 a.m. until 1:30 p.m. She stated at this workshop
  residents will learn about Reverse Mortgages, renters insurance, and the importance of
  burial cost. Lastly she stated an attorney will be present to discuss Wills and Trust.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  No name given, would like to convert her garage into a rental property but is having a
  few problems with doing so.

  Jason Peso commented he feels if the City implements rent control it will affect the Mom
  and Pop property owners. He suggested maybe the Council could look into raising the
  business tax and leaving the option of raising rents open.

  Gary Burket, representative of Platinum Billboards, LLC, presented the City of
  Inglewood with a check in the amount of $99,012.86, for advertising revenues generated
  from digital signage that hovers above the District 2 Community Center.

  Adriana Grimes, Staff Assistant, invited the residents of Inglewood to participate in the
  Document Shredding event in front of Inglewood High School starting at 9:00 a.m.

  3
 March 12, 2019

  Wayne Spencer, Chairman of South Bay Workforce Investment Board, briefed the
  Council and residents on what the organization is doing.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned at the hour of 2:32 p.m.

  Approved this 2nd day of April, 2019

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
